claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(D)=1 for which there exist an integer B>=2 and a nonempty finite set A of positive integers such that R={B^a:a in A} is contained in D, sigma(R)=sum_{d in R}1/(d-1)>=1/2, V=D minus R has min V>=4 and sigma(V)>1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit an integer N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once and coincident numerical values from different pairs retained separately.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3 with gcd(D)=1 for which there exist an integer B>=2 and a nonempty finite set A of positive integers such that R={B^a:a in A} is contained in D, sigma(R)=sum_{d in R}1/(d-1)>=1/2, V=D minus R has min V>=4 and sigma(V)>1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit an integer N(D,k,F) such that every integer n>=N is a sum of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once and coincident numerical values from different pairs retained separately.
quadruple.stage: Finite sets of integer bases, infinite ordered supplies of labelled pure powers, finite signed and positive subset sums, congruences and compact logarithmic rotations.

shape.objects: The finite labelled unit seed is extended by one fresh R-supported signed correction and exactly one eligible V power per step. Sections1--6 of moves/001-phase-modular-reserve.md prove a common extension for every finite state, on the complete admitted structural domain. No labelled-supply Mathlib encoding has been checked.
shape.quantifiers: Universal D, k and finite F, then existential N, then universal n>=N, then existential finite legal positive supports. The construction proposes finitely many disjoint signed unit pairs before N, not a probability or uncountable set-theoretic quantifier.
shape.target_quantity: Existence of eventual positive coverage for the exact structural family, a yes/no property settled by a finite but unspecified threshold N; no optimal constant or density bound is the target.
shape.ambient_structure: Integer order, additive occurrence capacity, congruences and a common-radix signed lattice. A period-multiple compact recurrence supplies each V correction while a single all-scale prefix ledger retains the original fixed reserve gap. All interfaces are proved without gcd(V)=1 in the analytical candidate.
shape.symmetries: Reordering base labels and choosing later unused occurrences preserve label capacity. A common-radix shift applies only on R. Arbitrary mixed-base dilation, subtraction of two signed representations and arbitrary block deletion need not preserve capacity or the reserve invariant.
shape.configuration: Required positive coverage with each label used at most once, finite disjoint signed unit pairs, and an unused reserve with one fixed gap chosen in advance. Truncating the supply destroys eventual coverage, and arbitrary seed-support removal can destroy the required fixed-gap invariant.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal candidate or optimized numerical threshold is sought.
shape.finite_certificates: A finite signed unit can be checked from its labels and exact integer difference. The smallest positive interval increment is one, from one unit pair, so the seed branch has a named smallest parameter without a process. Such a finite witness alone certifies neither the all-D eventual claim nor preservation for every scale. No finite equivalent residue for the whole claim is known.
shape.monotonicity: Coverage survives adding available labels and restricting to fewer forbidden labels. The theorem is stronger at larger cutoffs or larger finite forbidden sets. There is no scalar critical-parameter ladder or smallest remaining finite domain deciding this structural assertion.
shape.uniformity_parameter: The reserve gap must be independent of all later correction supports; D, k, F, the tail modulus and the required represented integer are unbounded. The proposed fixed phase tolerance depends only on V, not on the growing supports.
shape.proof_shape: A complete self-contained analytical candidate: prove interval amplification and the three-scale prefix invariant before a seed; establish the common-radix lattice and period-multiple phase return; construct g-1 disjoint unit pairs with one cumulative V ledger; combine their length-g positive interval with the final fixed-gap reserve. No conjectural preservation input remains in this local proof, pending independent exact-result review.
shape.neighbours: Known true locally: CP22 common-radix signed lattice and completeness after dedicating a whole correction base set, and CP26 one-label strict-mass prefix margin within its audited scope. Open: the present occurrence-reuse extension, equality complement mass, the original mass-one claim and arbitrary half-mass signed units. Failed related abstractions: node8 uncontrolled finite gadget support cost and node15 cutoff-dependent/scalar normalization. No relation reformulated as incidence, adjacency, rank, entropy or a known combinatorial principle solves this exact claim; no simpler ambient carries it verbatim.
shape.known_bounds: CP22 requires a collectively coprime whole correction set C and mass at least1 outside R union C. CP26 fixes its complement gap through individual near-aligned deletions, while its spectral conclusion needs gcd1 and only yields full-supply thickness. These necessary capacity and scope restrictions constrain any counterexample or construction here. No uniform barrier for the new combined operation, random first-moment estimate, complete finite residue or growing-support-independent finite certificate of the full claim is recorded.
shape.missing_input: None for the admitted structural claim in the local analytical candidate; independent result review and immutable acceptance remain due. The original mass-one claim, exact structural complement, equality and arbitrary half-mass cases remain open.
shape.base_theory: Classical mathematics in ZFC, with elementary integer arithmetic and compact metric group arguments. No axiom beyond this theory, uncountable independence or guessing principle is proposed. The analytical construction is intended to stay within ZFC; no machine or formal verification is claimed.
